title: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606)

officialDocument.title: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 syllabus for 2025, 2026 and 2027 (version 1, with the syllabus update of February 2024)
officialDocument.publisher: Cambridge University Press & Assessment (Cambridge International Education)

sourceNote: Topic headings and their numbers (1 to 14) are transcribed from the subject content of the official syllabus; objective codes are the syllabus's own content numbers (for example 10.5), and where several content numbers share one node the node code names them (for example 2.1-2.2). Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Read 2026-10-09 from the official PDF (version 1, for exams in 2025, 2026 and 2027): the 14 topics, every numbered content item with its notes and examples, the assessment overview, the details of the assessment, the List of formulas, the mathematical conventions, the command words and the list of changes.

Syllabus update applied: the separate update notice for this syllabus (dated February 2024) records only minor amendments to the marking principles in the mark schemes and updated specimen materials. It changes no subject content, papers, timings, marks or formulas, so nothing in this file differs because of it; content writers should follow the updated specimen mark schemes' marking principles (for example full justification and accuracy conventions).

Assessment as read: Paper 1, non-calculator (calculators not allowed), 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%; Paper 2, calculator (a scientific calculator is required), 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%. Both papers: structured and unstructured questions on any part of the content, all questions compulsory, externally marked. Grades A* to E (F and G not available). AO1 (knowledge and understanding of techniques) and AO2 (analyse, interpret and communicate) each 45-55% of each paper.

Conventions as read: non-exact answers to 3 significant figures and angles in degrees to 1 decimal place unless stated; exact answers in terms of π, e, ln, surds where asked; 'show that' needs full working; a List of formulas is printed (circle equation, cone and sphere formulas, quadratic formula, binomial theorem, arithmetic and geometric series, the three Pythagorean trigonometric identities, sine and cosine rules and the area of a triangle); no calculus formulas are given; arc-length and sector-area formulas are not given; trigonometric calculus uses radians.

Exclusions printed in the content: differentiation from first principles, points of inflexion, permutations with repeated objects or in a circle, problems needing both permutations and combinations, the greatest term and properties of binomial coefficients, and series expansions of eˣ and ln x. Indices and surds were removed as a topic for 2025 and are assumed knowledge from IGCSE Mathematics (not tested directly but needed in answers); the coordinate geometry of the circle was added and Paper 1 became a non-calculator paper.
This version runs to the 2027 examinations; create a new version file when the syllabus for 2028 onwards is published.

Not in this syllabus (taught in the family for ZIMSEC only): indices and exponential equations and surds as topics (assumed knowledge here), identities and unknown coefficients, linear inequalities, the behaviour of sequences, sigma notation, volumes of revolution, all of probability and statistics (probability, data, averages and dispersion, discrete and continuous random variables, binomial and normal distributions, sampling and estimation) and all of mechanics (kinematics with the equations of motion, forces, equilibrium, friction, Newton's laws, work, energy and power).
overview: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics stretches able IGCSE Mathematics learners and prepares them for AS & A Level Mathematics. It covers 14 topics of pure mathematics: functions; quadratic functions; factors of polynomials; equations, inequalities and graphs (including the modulus function and cubic graphs); simultaneous equations; logarithmic and exponential functions; straight-line graphs; the coordinate geometry of the circle; circular measure; trigonometry; permutations and combinations; series (binomial theorem, arithmetic and geometric progressions); vectors in two dimensions; and calculus (differentiation, integration and kinematics).
assessmentOverview: All candidates take Paper 1 (non-calculator, 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%) and Paper 2 (calculator, 2 hours, 80 marks, 50%). Both papers contain compulsory structured and unstructured questions on any part of the content. Grades A* to E.

components.name: Paper 1: Non-calculator
components.description: Structured and unstructured questions on any part of the content; all questions compulsory; calculators are not allowed.

components.name: Paper 2: Calculator
components.description: Structured and unstructured questions on any part of the content; all questions compulsory; a scientific calculator is required.

children.name: Functions: terms, domain, range and notation

objectives.text: Understand function, domain, range (image set), one-one and many-one functions, inverse and composite functions, and explain in words why a mapping is a function.
Find the domain and range of functions.
Recognise and use function notation.
Relate the graphs of y = f(x) and y = |f(x)| for linear, quadratic, cubic and trigonometric f(x).
Explain in words why a given function has no inverse.
Find the inverse of a one-one function, using correct notation.
Sketch a function and its inverse and show they are reflections in y = x.
Form and use composite functions, knowing that the order matters.

children.name: Maximum and minimum values and quadratic graphs

objectives.text: Find the maximum or minimum value of a quadratic function by completing the square or by differentiation.
Use the maximum or minimum value to sketch the graph or to find the range for a given domain.

children.name: The discriminant: roots and line–curve intersections

objectives.text: Know the discriminant conditions for two real, two equal or no real roots, and for a line to meet, touch or miss a curve.
Solve quadratic equations for real roots by factorising, the formula or completing the square.
Find the solution set of a quadratic inequality graphically or algebraically, written in the correct form.
Know and use the remainder and factor theorems.

children.name: Factors of polynomials and cubic equations

objectives.text: Find factors of polynomials, obtaining a linear and a quadratic factor of a cubic by observation or long division.
Solve cubic equations.
Solve equations involving the modulus of linear and quadratic expressions algebraically or graphically.
Solve inequalities involving the modulus of linear and quadratic expressions graphically or algebraically.
Use a substitution to form and solve a quadratic equation in order to solve a related equation.
Sketch cubic graphs given as a product of three linear factors, and their moduli.
Solve cubic inequalities graphically.
Solve simultaneous equations in two unknowns by elimination or substitution.

children.name: Properties and graphs of logarithmic and exponential functions

objectives.text: Know and use the properties and graphs of logarithmic and exponential functions, including ln x and eˣ and their asymptotes.
Know and use the laws of logarithms, including change of base.

children.name: Equations of the form aˣ = b

objectives.text: Solve equations of the form aˣ = b.

children.name: The equation of a straight line

objectives.text: Use the equation of a straight line.

children.name: Parallel and perpendicular lines; midpoints, lengths and perpendicular bisectors

objectives.text: Know and use the conditions for two lines to be parallel or perpendicular.
Solve problems with midpoints and lengths of lines, including the perpendicular bisector.
Transform relationships to and from straight-line form and find unknown constants from the gradient or intercept.
Know and use the equation of a circle with given centre and radius, in any form.
Solve problems on the intersection of a circle and a straight line.
Solve problems involving tangents to a circle.
Solve problems on the intersection of two circles.

children.name: Arc length and sector area in radians

objectives.text: Solve problems on arc length and sector area, including compound shapes, using radian measure.
Know and use the six trigonometric functions of angles of any magnitude.
Understand and use the amplitude and period of a trigonometric function and relate the graphs of related functions.
Draw and use the graphs of y = a sin bx + c, y = a cos bx + c and y = a tan bx + c.
Use the Pythagorean identities in sin and cos, sec and tan, and cosec and cot.
Prove trigonometric relationships involving the six functions.
Solve trigonometric equations involving the six functions in a given domain, using the identities where needed.
Recognise the difference between permutations and combinations and know when to use each.
Know and use n! and the expressions for permutations and combinations of n items taken r at a time.
Solve arrangement and selection problems with permutations or combinations.
Use the binomial theorem to expand (a + b)ⁿ for a positive integer n.
Use the general term of a binomial expansion, for example to find a term independent of x.
Recognise arithmetic and geometric progressions and the difference between them.
Use the nth-term and sum formulas to solve problems on arithmetic and geometric progressions.
Use the condition for a geometric progression to converge and the formula for its sum to infinity.

children.name: Vector notation, position and unit vectors, magnitude and operations

objectives.text: Understand and use vector notation.
Know and use position vectors and unit vectors.
Find the magnitude of a vector, add and subtract vectors and multiply them by scalars, including vector geometry.
Compose and resolve velocities, including position from a velocity vector.

children.name: The derived function and its notation

objectives.text: Understand the idea of a derived function (informally, without first principles).
Use the notations for first and second derivatives.

children.name: Derivatives of standard functions and the chain rule

objectives.text: Know and use the derivatives of xⁿ, sin x, cos x, tan x, eˣ and ln x, with constant multiples, sums and the chain rule.
Differentiate products and quotients of functions.
Use differentiation to find gradients, tangents and normals.
Use differentiation to find stationary points.
Use the first and second derivative tests to tell maxima from minima, with full justification.

children.name: Connected rates of change, small increments and approximations

objectives.text: Apply differentiation to connected rates of change, small increments and approximations.
Apply differentiation to practical problems involving maxima and minima.

children.name: Integration as the reverse of differentiation

objectives.text: Understand integration as the reverse process of differentiation.
Integrate sums of terms in powers of x, including 1/x and 1/(ax + b).
Integrate (ax + b)ⁿ for rational n, sin(ax + b), cos(ax + b), sec²(ax + b) and e^(ax+b).
Evaluate definite integrals and find plane areas, including between a line and a curve and between two curves.
Apply differentiation and integration to the displacement, velocity and acceleration of a particle moving in a straight line.
Draw and use displacement–time, distance–time, velocity–time, speed–time and acceleration–time graphs.
